## Where the day goes

Two halves. The morning fits models to survey data and interprets them for a
non-technical reader. The afternoon puts district-level estimates onto Pakistan.

|---|---|---|
| 1 | Linear and logistic regression, interpreted | [`scripts/linear-regression.R`](scripts/linear-regression.R), [`scripts/car-price-regression.R`](scripts/car-price-regression.R) |
| 2 | Weighted demographic indicators from DHS/MICS | [`01-dhs-model-datasets.qmd`](01-dhs-model-datasets.qmd), [`scripts/pdhs-indicators.R`](scripts/pdhs-indicators.R) |
| 3 | Boundaries, joins, choropleths | [`scripts/pakistan-district-choropleth.R`](scripts/pakistan-district-choropleth.R) |

## Scripts in this folder

- `mics-child.R` — child indicators from MICS
- `survey-health-indicators.R` — fertility, mortality and child health together
- `fertility-analysis.R` — a longer worked fertility analysis

## The joining problem

`pakistan-district-choropleth.R` is the session that teaches the real lesson of
spatial work: district names in a survey almost never match district names in a
shapefile. The script uses `fuzzyjoin` and then checks the residual non-matches by
hand. Do not skip the checking step — a silent 12% drop is how maps end up wrong.

## What you should be able to do by 16:30

- fit a weighted model and report it without over-claiming
- explain a coefficient to a policymaker in one sentence
- join survey estimates to a shapefile and verify the join
- produce a choropleth and a leaflet map
